claim: CHO centrioles were on average 440 nm long
source: These CHO centrioles were on average 440 nm long, and appeared to taper along their length, being wider at the proximal end, which would be connected to the central hub, and narrower at the distal end which, in a basal body, would face the membrane (Figure 1a).
evidence: The claim is supported by measurements from electron cryo-tomography data of CHO centrioles, as shown in Figure 1a.

claim: CHO centrioles appeared to taper along their length, being wider at the proximal end and narrower at the distal end
source: These CHO centrioles were on average 440 nm long, and appeared to taper along their length, being wider at the proximal end, which would be connected to the central hub, and narrower at the distal end which, in a basal body, would face the membrane (Figure 1a).
evidence: The claim is based on direct observation from tomograms shown in Figure 1a.

claim: The CHO centriole consisted of a TMT having a 13 protofilament A-tubule and 10 protofilament B- and C-tubules
source: Consistent with previously published data from basal bodies (Guichard et al., 2013; Li et al., 2012), the CHO centriole consisted of a TMT having a 13 protofilament A-tubule and 10 protofilament B- and C-tubules.
evidence: The claim is supported by sub-volume averaging data from CHO centrioles and is consistent with previously published data from basal bodies.

claim: The global CHO TMT map was generated at ~3.5 nm resolution
source: This produced a dataset that contained ~2100 unique subvolumes, which were aligned to a common reference (see Methods) and averaged to generate a global map of the CHO TMT (Figure 1b) (EMD-7775) at ~3.5 nm resolution (Figure 1—figure supplement 2)
evidence: The resolution is determined from gold standard FSC plots shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 2.

claim: Local resolution metrics indicate that the majority of the CHO TMT volume has a resolution between 2.4 and 2.8 nm
source: This produced a dataset that contained ~2100 unique subvolumes, which were aligned to a common reference (see Methods) and averaged to generate a global map of the CHO TMT (Figure 1b) (EMD-7775) at ~3.5 nm resolution (Figure 1—figure supplement 2) although local resolution metrics indicate that the majority of the volume has a resolution between 2.4 and 2.8 nm (Figure 1—figure supplement 3).
evidence: The claim is supported by ResMap resolution calculations shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 3.

claim: The lack of cartwheel spokes attaching to the pinhead is in agreement with published work suggesting that the cartwheel is specific to procentrioles and removed during the progression from mitosis to interphase
source: Given the high degree of structural preservation using cryoET, the lack of cartwheel spokes attaching to the pinhead is in agreement with published work suggesting that the cartwheel is specific to procentrioles and removed during the progression from mitosis to interphase (Vorobjev and Chentsov, 1980; Arquint and Nigg, 2014).
evidence: The claim is based on the absence of cartwheel spokes in the cryoET data and is supported by citations to previous work.

claim: Four microtubule-internal proteins (MIPs) were observed on the luminal surfaces of the CHO TMTs
source: At this resolution, we observed four microtubule-internal proteins (MIPs) on the luminal surfaces of the TMTs (Figure 1b).
evidence: The claim is based on direct observation in the sub-volume average shown in Figure 1b.

claim: The most prominent MIP within the A-tubule straddles a gap between the A09 and A10 protofilaments
source: The most prominent was within the A-tubule, straddling a gap between the A09 and A10 protofilaments (Figure 1b and c), a gap that was much larger than between any of the other protofilaments of the A-tubule (asterisk in Figure 1c).
evidence: The claim is based on direct observation in the sub-volume averages shown in Figures 1b and 1c.

claim: Recent single-particle cryoEM data on cilia assigned the microtubule seam between the A09 and A10 protofilaments
source: Recent single-particle cryoEM data on cilia assigned the microtubule seam between the A09 and A10 protofilaments (Ichikawa et al., 2017).
evidence: The claim is supported by citation to a previous study.

claim: The large A-tubule MIP is binding along the internal surface of the A-tubule at the unique microtubule seam
source: This suggested that the large A-tubule MIP is binding along the internal surface of the A-tubule at the unique microtubule seam.
evidence: The claim is inferred from the position of the MIP at the gap between A09 and A10 protofilaments, which is identified as the seam location based on cited work.

claim: All centrioles in the CHO dataset were significantly flattened
source: This refitting revealed that all centrioles in our dataset were significantly flattened.
evidence: The claim is based on refitting the average back into the raw data, as shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 4.

claim: Some CHO centrioles more closely resembled two parallel arrays of triplet microtubules than the stereotypical 9-fold symmetric structure
source: While the degree of flattening varied between datasets, some centrioles more closely resembled two parallel arrays of triplet microtubules than the stereotypical 9-fold symmetric structure that was expected (Figure 1—figure supplement 4).
evidence: The claim is based on refitting analysis shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 4.

claim: The ellipticity of the A-tubule in the CHO TMT average was measured to have ~10% distortion
source: We measured the ellipticity of the A-tubule in our TMT average to have ~10% distortion, in keeping with previously published values for basal bodies and axonemes (Li et al., 2012; Sui and Downing, 2006).
evidence: The claim is based on measurements from the TMT average and is consistent with previously published values.

claim: The A- and B-tubules and their respective MIPs represent the core structure of the TMT at high-contour threshold
source: Analysis of the TMT global map at a high-contour threshold indicated that apart from the A- and B-tubules, and their respective MIPs, most other features in the map were at less than full occupancy (Figure 1c).
evidence: The claim is based on analysis of the global map at high contour threshold shown in Figure 1c.

claim: The A-C linker and pinhead were completely absent at high contour level in the CHO TMT global map
source: At this contour level, the A-C linker (Figure 1c - green double arrowheads) and pinhead (Figure 1c - gold arrow) were completely absent, as was part of the C-tubule.
evidence: The claim is based on analysis of the global map at high contour threshold shown in Figure 1c.

claim: The absence of the pinhead at high contour is consistent with previous work where the pinhead did not persist along the entire length of the centriole
source: This is consistent with previous work where the pinhead did not persist along the entire length of the centriole (Paintrand et al., 1992).
evidence: The claim is supported by citation to previous work.

claim: CHO centrioles are formed from two approximately equally-sized domains: a proximal domain and a distal domain
source: These proximal-distal axis averages showed that the centrioles were formed from two approximately equally-sized domains: a proximal domain, where complete TMTs contained a clear pinhead and A-C linker (Figure 2a and b), and a distal domain, where the pinhead, the A-C linker, and part of the C-tubule were missing (Figure 2c and d).
evidence: The claim is based on proximal-distal axis averaging shown in Figure 2.

claim: The proximal domain of CHO centrioles contains complete TMTs with a clear pinhead and A-C linker
source: These proximal-distal axis averages showed that the centrioles were formed from two approximately equally-sized domains: a proximal domain, where complete TMTs contained a clear pinhead and A-C linker (Figure 2a and b), and a distal domain, where the pinhead, the A-C linker, and part of the C-tubule were missing (Figure 2c and d).
evidence: The claim is based on proximal-distal axis averaging shown in Figures 2a and 2b.

claim: The distal domain of CHO centrioles lacks the pinhead, the A-C linker, and part of the C-tubule
source: These proximal-distal axis averages showed that the centrioles were formed from two approximately equally-sized domains: a proximal domain, where complete TMTs contained a clear pinhead and A-C linker (Figure 2a and b), and a distal domain, where the pinhead, the A-C linker, and part of the C-tubule were missing (Figure 2c and d).
evidence: The claim is based on proximal-distal axis averaging shown in Figures 2c and 2d.

claim: In the distal half of the CHO centriole, a large and unique density emanates from the inner side of the A-tubule in the absence of the pinhead
source: In the absence of the pinhead, the distal half of the centriole showed a large and unique density emanating from the inner side of the A-tubule (Figure 2c and d - gold double arrowheads).
evidence: The claim is based on proximal-distal axis averaging shown in Figures 2c and 2d.

claim: The proximal and distal CHO centriole averages maintained ~3.5 nm resolution despite containing only half the number of subvolumes
source: Even though each set only contained half the number of subvolumes, the ~3.5 nm resolution was maintained, allowing us to gain additional structural insights into centriole organization (Figure 3) (EMD-7776, EMD-7777).
evidence: The claim is based on resolution determination from the proximal and distal averages.

claim: The large A-tubule MIP straddling protofilaments A09 and A10 is equally strong in both proximal and distal CHO centriole averages
source: In addition to the large structural changes, we also noted that while the large A-tubule MIP straddling protofilaments A09 and A10 was equally strong in both proximal and distal averages, the A-tubule MIP on protofilament A11 was absent in the distal centriole (Figure 3a/d and and b/c).
evidence: The claim is based on comparison of proximal and distal averages shown in Figure 3.

claim: The A-tubule MIP on protofilament A11 is absent in the distal CHO centriole
source: In addition to the large structural changes, we also noted that while the large A-tubule MIP straddling protofilaments A09 and A10 was equally strong in both proximal and distal averages, the A-tubule MIP on protofilament A11 was absent in the distal centriole (Figure 3a/d and and b/c).
evidence: The claim is based on comparison of proximal and distal averages shown in Figure 3.

claim: The distal CHO centriole map has a very large novel L-shaped density that extends from the inner AB-junction and points towards the lumen of the centriole
source: The most surprising element of the distal-centriole map was the presence of a very large novel L-shaped density that extended from the inner AB-junction, and pointed towards the lumen of the centriole (Figure 3b - green arrow).
evidence: The claim is based on the distal centriole average shown in Figure 3b.

claim: The L-shaped density in the distal CHO centriole is structurally and positionally unrelated to the pinhead but occupies much the same space
source: The origin of this L-shaped density was structurally and positionally unrelated to the pinhead, but occupied much the same space, indicating that these structures must be mutually exclusive.
evidence: The claim is based on comparison of the proximal and distal averages and inference about mutual exclusivity.

claim: The proximal CHO centriole has a compact inner AB-junction that mediates A-tubule to B-tubule binding
source: The inner AB-junctions showed that while the proximal centriole has a compact junction that mediates A-tubule to B-tubule binding (Figure 3d - dashed white circle), the inner AB-junction in the distal centriole was much more elaborate (Figure 3e - dashed white circle).
evidence: The claim is based on the proximal centriole average shown in Figure 3d.

claim: The inner AB-junction in the distal CHO centriole is much more elaborate than in the proximal centriole
source: The inner AB-junctions showed that while the proximal centriole has a compact junction that mediates A-tubule to B-tubule binding (Figure 3d - dashed white circle), the inner AB-junction in the distal centriole was much more elaborate (Figure 3e - dashed white circle).
evidence: The claim is based on comparison of proximal and distal averages shown in Figures 3d and 3e.

claim: The distal AB-junction has additional globular domains binding to protofilaments A01/A02 that act as a platform from which the L-shaped density extends
source: In addition to forming the junction between the A- and B-tubules, the distal AB-junction appeared to have additional globular domains binding to protofilaments A01/A02 that acted as a platform from which the L-shaped density extended (Figure 3e - dashed white circle).
evidence: The claim is based on the distal centriole average shown in Figure 3e.

claim: The geometry from previously published data on centrosomes isolated from human lymphoblasts was used to circumvent the flattening observed in CHO centrioles
source: To circumvent the flattening, we used the geometry from previously published data on centrosomes isolated from human lymphoblasts, where centrioles embedded in resin showed no signs of flattening (Paintrand et al., 1992).
evidence: The claim is based on the methodology used to correct for flattening, citing previous work.

claim: Imposing the published proximal symmetry to the averaged proximal CHO map recreated a 9-fold symmetry with a diameter of ~235 nm
source: Imposing the published proximal symmetry to our averaged proximal map recreated a 9-fold symmetry that satisfied TMT linkages via the A-C linker (Figure 4a,c - orange arrowheads) and the diameter of the ensemble structure was ~235 nm.
evidence: The claim is based on applying published symmetry to the proximal map, as shown in Figure 4a and 4c.

claim: The overall diameter of the distal CHO centriole decreased to ~220 nm
source: The overall diameter of the distal centriole had decreased to ~220 nm, a change achieved by a rotation of the triplets inwards by ~15˚.
evidence: The claim is based on applying published distal symmetry to the distal map.

claim: The change in diameter from the proximal to distal CHO centriole accounts for the centriole tapering initially observed in the tomograms
source: This change in diameter from the proximal centriole accounts for the centriole tapering that we initially observed in the tomograms (Figure 1a).
evidence: The claim is inferred from the diameter measurements and the initial observation of tapering.

claim: In the distal CHO centriole, the L-shaped density from the inner AB-junction of one triplet zigzags across and connects to the inner AB-junction of the adjacent triplet
source: In particular, the L-shaped density emanating from the inner AB-junction of one triplet zigzagged across and connected to the inner AB-junction of the adjacent triplet (Figure 4d - blue arrowhead).
evidence: The claim is based on the distal centriole map with applied symmetry shown in Figure 4d.

claim: On the external surface of the distal CHO centriole A-tubule, a foot-like appendage extends from protofilament A09 and binds to protofilaments C07/C08 of the adjacent triplet
source: On the external surface of the A-tubule, a foot-like appendage extended from protofilament A09 and appeared to bind directly to protofilaments C07/C08 the C-tubule of the adjacent triplet (Figure 4d - green arrowhead), generating a non-canonical A-C linker and simultaneously stabilizing the shape and location of the end of the partial C-tubule sheet.
evidence: The claim is based on the distal centriole map with applied symmetry shown in Figure 4d.

claim: In the distal CHO centriole, two new structures and a partial C-tubule mediate the linkage of adjacent triplets in the absence of the canonical A-C linker
source: Thus, in the absence of the canonical A-C linker in the distal centriole, two new structures and a partial C-tubule mediate the linkage of adjacent triplets, while altering the geometry of the distal centriole to be more axoneme like.
evidence: The claim is inferred from the structural features observed in the distal centriole map.

claim: Drosophila S2 centrioles were much shorter than CHO centrioles, with an average length of ~175 nm
source: Drosophila S2 centrioles were much shorter than the CHO centrioles, with an average length of ~175 nm.
evidence: The claim is based on measurements from cryoET data of Drosophila S2 centrioles.

claim: Fly centrioles are composed of predominantly DMT, although SMTs and DMTs can be observed within the same centriole
source: In end-on views, it was clear that fly centrioles were composed of predominantly DMT, although SMTs and DMTs could be observed within the same centriole (Figure 5a).
evidence: The claim is based on end-on views of fly centrioles shown in Figure 5a.

claim: The SMTs and DMTs in fly centrioles are symmetrically arranged around a central hub
source: The SMTs and DMTs were symmetrically arranged around a central hub (Figure 5a).
evidence: The claim is based on end-on views of fly centrioles shown in Figure 5a.

claim: End-on fly centrioles showed brush-like structures extending out from the cytoplasmic face of the centrioles, concentrated in the regions between the DMTs
source: Intriguingly, end-on centrioles showed brush-like structures, likely representing the core PCM, extending out from the cytoplasmic face of the centrioles and concentrated in the regions between the DMTs (Figure 5a – white arrows).
evidence: The claim is based on end-on views of fly centrioles shown in Figure 5a.

claim: The global map of fly DMTs was generated at ~3.5 nm resolution
source: This gave a dataset of ~3000 unique sub-volumes, which were aligned to a common reference and averaged to generate a global map of the fly DMTs (Figure 5) at ~3.5 nm resolution (EMD-7778) (Figure 1—figure supplement 2).
evidence: The resolution is determined from gold standard FSC plots shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 2.

claim: The fly DMT is composed of a 13 protofilament A-tubule and a 10 protofilament B-tubule
source: As expected, this averaging generated a DMT, composed of a 13 protofilament A-tubule and a 10 protofilament B-tubule (Figure 5b).
evidence: The claim is based on sub-volume averaging shown in Figure 5b.

claim: The fly DMT map shows a single prominent MIP bound to the luminal surface of the A09/A10 protofilaments, indistinguishable from the A-tubule MIP in the CHO map
source: The map showed a single prominent MIP bound to the luminal surface of the A09/A10 protofilaments; its shape and position were indistinguishable from the A-tubule MIP that we identified in the CHO map (compare with Figure 1b).
evidence: The claim is based on comparison of the fly DMT map (Figure 5b) with the CHO TMT map (Figure 1b).

claim: The B-tubule MIP bridging the B01 and B02 protofilaments observed in mammalian centrioles is absent from the fly B-tubule
source: In contrast, the B-tubule MIP bridging the B01 and B02 protofilaments observed in the mammalian centrioles (Figure 1b) was absent from the fly B-tubule.
evidence: The claim is based on comparison of the fly DMT map with the CHO TMT map.

claim: The fly B-tubule curvature is indistinguishable from that of the CHO B-tubule despite the absence of the B01/B02 MIP
source: Despite this, the fly B-tubule curvature was otherwise indistinguishable from that of the CHO B-tubule, suggesting that a B-tubule MIP is dispensable.
evidence: The claim is based on comparison of the fly and CHO B-tubule structures.

claim: The connection between A11 and B01 is maintained in fly centrioles even in the absence of the B01/B02 MIP
source: Furthermore, the connection between A11 and B01 is maintained in fly centrioles, even in the absence of the B01/B02 MIP, and is perhaps sufficient for B-tubule construction.
evidence: The claim is based on observation of the fly DMT structure and inference about B-tubule construction.

claim: The pinhead in the fly DMT is much more elaborate than the CHO pinhead, making additional contacts with the A02 protofilament and the inner AB-junction
source: A pinhead that extended from the A03 protofilament (Figure 5b – white arrow) was much more elaborate than the CHO pinhead, doubling back to make additional contacts with the A02 protofilament and the inner AB-junction (Figure 5b – green double arrowhead).
evidence: The claim is based on the fly DMT map shown in Figure 5b.

claim: The fly DMT map shows a hinge-like density extending from the A05/A06 protofilaments
source: In addition to the elaborated pinhead, our DMT maps showed two novel densities that were not observed in the CHO TMTs; a hinge-like density extended from the A05/A06 protofilaments (Figure 5b – gold double arrowhead), and a wishbone-shaped structure (Figure 5b pink double arrowheads) that made weak connections with protofilament A08.
evidence: The claim is based on the fly DMT map shown in Figure 5b.

claim: The fly DMT map shows a wishbone-shaped structure that makes weak connections with protofilament A08
source: In addition to the elaborated pinhead, our DMT maps showed two novel densities that were not observed in the CHO TMTs; a hinge-like density extended from the A05/A06 protofilaments (Figure 5b – gold double arrowhead), and a wishbone-shaped structure (Figure 5b pink double arrowheads) that made weak connections with protofilament A08.
evidence: The claim is based on the fly DMT map shown in Figure 5b.

claim: At high-level threshold in the fly DMT map, the only elements that remained are the A-tubule, pinhead and parts of the B-tubule
source: An analysis of the fly DMT map at high-level threshold indicated that not all structural elements were at 100% occupancy (Figure 5c), as was the case for the CHO TMT. Indeed, the only elements that remained at high-level threshold were the A-tubule, pinhead and parts of the B-tubule.
evidence: The claim is based on analysis of the fly DMT map at high contour threshold shown in Figure 5c.

claim: The clear presence of the pinhead but lack of an L-shaped density extending from the inner AB-junction suggests that the fly centriole does not form the distal domain identified in the CHO centriole
source: The clear presence of the pinhead (Figure 5c - white arrow) but lack of an L-shaped density extending from the inner AB-junction, suggests that the fly centriole does not form the distal domain that we identified in the CHO centriole.
evidence: The claim is inferred from the presence of pinhead and absence of L-shaped density in the fly DMT map.

claim: In the fly DMT B-tubule, density is weakest for protofilaments B03-B06, while B01-B02 and B08-B10 show much stronger density
source: In the case of the fly, DMT B-tubule density was weakest for protofilaments B03-B06, while B01-B02 and B08-B10 showed much stronger density (Figure 5c), suggesting differences in density between the B-tubule of the S2 centriole, and the C-tubule of the CHO centriole.
evidence: The claim is based on analysis of the fly DMT map at high contour threshold shown in Figure 5c.

claim: Two fly centrioles whose axis was oriented orthogonal to the ice sheet showed no obvious flattening
source: However, due to the fact that S2 centrioles are approximately half the length of the CHO centrioles, we imaged two centrioles whose axis was oriented orthogonal to the ice sheet, presenting an end-on view (2 of 30). These end-on centrioles showed no obvious flattening and their geometry closely matched the geometry of the flattening-corrected proximal CHO centriole, with the angles of the DMTs being remarkably similar to those of the CHO TMTs (Figure 6—figure supplement 1).
evidence: The claim is based on end-on views of fly centrioles shown in Figure 6—figure supplement 1.

claim: The geometry of end-on fly centrioles closely matched the geometry of the flattening-corrected proximal CHO centriole
source: These end-on centrioles showed no obvious flattening and their geometry closely matched the geometry of the flattening-corrected proximal CHO centriole, with the angles of the DMTs being remarkably similar to those of the CHO TMTs (Figure 6—figure supplement 1).
evidence: The claim is based on comparison of end-on fly centrioles with the proximal CHO centriole geometry shown in Figure 6—figure supplement 1.

claim: The diameter of S2 centrioles is smaller than CHO centrioles (~210 nm vs. ~235 nm, respectively)
source: The diameter of S2 centrioles was smaller than CHO centrioles (~210 nm vs. ~235 nm, respectively), a difference that can be accounted for by the absence of the C-tubules.
evidence: The claim is based on measurements from reconstructed centrioles.

claim: The difference in diameter between S2 and CHO centrioles can be accounted for by the absence of the C-tubules in S2 centrioles
source: The diameter of S2 centrioles was smaller than CHO centrioles (~210 nm vs. ~235 nm, respectively), a difference that can be accounted for by the absence of the C-tubules.
evidence: The claim is inferred from the structural differences between S2 and CHO centrioles.

claim: Fly DMTs are connected through their A-tubules alone, using a novel A-A linker
source: The reconstructed centriole (Figure 6a) revealed that fly DMTs are connected through their A-tubules alone, using a novel A-A linker instead of a modified or elongated A-C linker.
evidence: The claim is based on the reconstructed fly centriole shown in Figure 6a.

claim: The A-A linker in fly centrioles consists of the hinge-like density emanating from the A05/A06 protofilaments of one DMT, extending and connecting to the side of the elaborated pinhead of an adjacent DMT
source: This A-A linker consisted of the hinge-like density (similar in shape to the malleus bone of the inner ear) emanating from the A05/A06 protofilaments of one DMT, extending and connecting to the side of the elaborated pinhead of an adjacent DMT (Figure 6b - gold double arrowhead).
evidence: The claim is based on the reconstructed fly centriole shown in Figure 6b.

claim: The wishbone-shaped structure in the fly DMT more closely resembles a hollow cone between adjacent DMTs when seen in context
source: The 9-fold refit also showed that the wishbone-shaped structure observed in the DMT average (Figure 5b - pink double arrowheads), more closely resembled a hollow cone between adjacent DMTs when seen in context (Figure 6b - pink double arrowheads).
evidence: The claim is based on the 9-fold refit shown in Figure 6b.

claim: The hollow cone structure in fly centrioles makes weak connections back to the A-A linker and the cytoplasmic face of protofilament A08
source: In addition, this density made weak connections back to the A-A linker and the cytoplasmic face of protofilament A08.
evidence: The claim is based on the 9-fold refit shown in Figure 6b.

claim: The hollow cone structure in fly centrioles likely represents the attachment of core PCM factors to the external surface of the centriole
source: While this structure is poorly defined and at less than 100% occupancy, its location is consistent with the brush-like structures we observed in the raw data, and likely represents the attachment of core PCM factors to the external surface of the centriole.
evidence: The claim is inferred from the location and appearance of the structure.

claim: Incomplete B-tubules in the fly centriole have previously been described and are thought to represent construction intermediates in the rapidly dividing embryo
source: Incomplete B-tubules in the fly centriole have previously been described and are thought to represent construction intermediates in the rapidly dividing embryo (Callaini et al., 1997; Moritz et al., 1995).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to previous work.

claim: Classification of the fly B-tubule gave a class in which microtubule sheets curve inward from both the inner- and outer-AB junctions
source: Using 3D classification (see Materials and methods), we grouped together all subvolumes that lacked protofilaments B03-B06 and generated a new average (EMD-7779). Even though this was a small number of subvolume (N = 226), there was clear, coherent density for the flanking protofilaments, B01-B02 and B07-B10 (Figure 7a).
evidence: The claim is based on 3D classification and averaging shown in Figure 7a.

claim: The flanking segments of the incomplete fly B-tubule have approximately the same curvature as the complete B-tubule
source: The flanking segments of the incomplete B-tubule have approximately the same curvature as the complete B-tubule.
evidence: The claim is based on analysis of the partial B-tubule average.

claim: The partial B-tubules in fly centrioles represent a kinetic intermediate in the formation of a complete B tubule
source: Together the data suggest that the partial B-tubules represent a kinetic intermediate in the formation of a complete B tubule.
evidence: The claim is inferred from the structural features of the partial B-tubules.

claim: The B-tubule in fly centrioles is constructed by first forming microtubule stubs at each joint on the A-tubule (B01/B02 and B07-B10), subsequently growing together to form a complete B-tubule
source: That is, the B-tubule would be constructed by first forming microtubule stubs at each joint on the A-tubule (B01/B02 and B07-B10), subsequently growing together to form a complete B-tubule.
evidence: The claim is a model inferred from the partial B-tubule structures.

claim: Entire rods in fly centrioles tend to be composed of either complete or partial DMTs, not simply the ends of each DMT rod
source: The data suggest that entire rods tend to be composed of either complete or partial DMTs, not simply the ends of each DMT rod.
evidence: The claim is based on refitting analysis shown in Figure 7b.

claim: Mammalian and fly centrioles have a broadly similar quasi-9-fold symmetrical cylindrical architecture
source: Our data show that, although mammalian and fly centrioles have a broadly similar quasi-9-fold symmetrical cylindrical architecture, the linkages between centriole microtubules that achieve this architecture are completely different.
evidence: The claim is a summary conclusion based on the structural data presented.

claim: The linkages between centriole microtubules in mammalian and fly centrioles are completely different
source: Our data show that, although mammalian and fly centrioles have a broadly similar quasi-9-fold symmetrical cylindrical architecture, the linkages between centriole microtubules that achieve this architecture are completely different.
evidence: The claim is a summary conclusion based on the structural data presented.

claim: The longer mammalian centriole is organized into two distinct domains along its proximal-distal axis
source: Furthermore, the longer mammalian centriole is organized into two distinct domains along its proximal-distal axis: a proximal domain, whose composition of interconnected triplets shares geometry with the fly centriole, and a distal domain comprised of novel linkages between centriole microtubules, generating a geometry that is intermediate between that of the proximal centriole and an axoneme.
evidence: The claim is a summary conclusion based on the structural data presented.

claim: The proximal domain of the mammalian centriole shares geometry with the fly centriole
source: Furthermore, the longer mammalian centriole is organized into two distinct domains along its proximal-distal axis: a proximal domain, whose composition of interconnected triplets shares geometry with the fly centriole, and a distal domain comprised of novel linkages between centriole microtubules, generating a geometry that is intermediate between that of the proximal centriole and an axoneme.
evidence: The claim is a summary conclusion based on comparison of mammalian and fly centriole structures.

claim: The distal domain of the mammalian centriole generates a geometry that is intermediate between that of the proximal centriole and an axoneme
source: Furthermore, the longer mammalian centriole is organized into two distinct domains along its proximal-distal axis: a proximal domain, whose composition of interconnected triplets shares geometry with the fly centriole, and a distal domain comprised of novel linkages between centriole microtubules, generating a geometry that is intermediate between that of the proximal centriole and an axoneme.
evidence: The claim is a summary conclusion based on the structural data presented.

claim: The distal mammalian centriole provides a transitional region that allows for the templating of both motile and sensory axonemes
source: Together our data suggest a model where the distal mammalian centriole provides a transitional region that allows for the templating of both motile and sensory axonemes, a region and potential that does not exist in somatic fly centrioles.
evidence: The claim is a model proposed based on the structural data and functional considerations.

claim: The transitional region in the distal mammalian centriole does not exist in somatic fly centrioles
source: Together our data suggest a model where the distal mammalian centriole provides a transitional region that allows for the templating of both motile and sensory axonemes, a region and potential that does not exist in somatic fly centrioles.
evidence: The claim is inferred from the absence of the distal domain in fly centrioles.

claim: The 9-fold symmetry of all motile and nonmotile cilia is universally conserved in all organisms thus far studied
source: The 9-fold symmetry of all motile and nonmotile cilia is universally conserved in all organisms thus far studied.
evidence: The claim is based on established scientific knowledge.

claim: The decoration of motile cilia with dyneins and radial spokes differentiates motile cilia from sensory cilia both structurally and functionally
source: However, the decoration of motile cilia with dyneins and radial spokes differentiates motile cilia from sensory cilia both structurally and functionally.
evidence: The claim is based on established scientific knowledge.

claim: Bioinformatic data suggest that the ancestral eukaryotic centriole was composed of triplet microtubules
source: Bioinformatic data suggest that the ancestral eukaryotic centriole was composed of triplet microtubules; this architecture has been maintained across the evolutionary spectrum in organisms ranging from trypanosomes to mammals (Carvalho-Santos et al., 2011).
evidence: The claim is supported by citation to previous work.

claim: The ancestral triplet microtubule architecture has been maintained across the evolutionary spectrum in organisms ranging from trypanosomes to mammals
source: Bioinformatic data suggest that the ancestral eukaryotic centriole was composed of triplet microtubules; this architecture has been maintained across the evolutionary spectrum in organisms ranging from trypanosomes to mammals (Carvalho-Santos et al., 2011).
evidence: The claim is supported by citation to previous work.

claim: Previous studies have established that adjacent triplet microtubules in basal bodies are linked through an A-C linker connecting A09 with C08/C09
source: Previous studies have established that adjacent triplet microtubules in basal bodies are linked through an A-C linker connecting A09 with C08/C09 (Carvalho-Santos et al., 2011; Guichard et al., 2013; Li et al., 2012; Paintrand et al., 1992).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to previous work.

claim: A similar A-A linker connection strategy may be employed in other organisms without TMTs, such as C. elegans
source: A similar connection strategy may very well be employed in other organisms without TMTs, such as C. elegans.
evidence: The claim is speculative, based on the discovery of the A-A linker in Drosophila.

claim: The A-A linker in fly centrioles serves as the primary anchor point for the surrounding PCM
source: Moreover, this linkage also appears to serve as the primary anchor point for the surrounding PCM (Figures 5a and 6b) connecting either directly or indirectly to proteins such as Asl and Plp (Fu and Glover, 2012; Mennella et al., 2012; Roque et al., 2018).
evidence: The claim is inferred from the location of the A-A linker and supported by citations to previous work on PCM proteins.

claim: Evolution puts a premium on maintaining the geometry of the centriole
source: Given the diversity in the linkages, yet the maintenance of the geometry, it is clear that evolution puts a premium on maintaining the geometry of the centriole, an organization that is instructive in determining cilium geometry.
evidence: The claim is inferred from the observation of conserved geometry despite diverse linkages.

claim: Centriole geometry is instructive in determining cilium geometry
source: Given the diversity in the linkages, yet the maintenance of the geometry, it is clear that evolution puts a premium on maintaining the geometry of the centriole, an organization that is instructive in determining cilium geometry.
evidence: The claim is inferred from the conserved geometry and its relationship to cilium structure.

claim: All centrioles share a common core, ~200 nm in length
source: These data suggest that all centrioles share a common core,~200 nm in length, but that mammalian centrioles are distally extended.
evidence: The claim is inferred from comparison of mammalian and fly centriole structures.

claim: Mammalian centrioles are distally extended beyond the common core
source: These data suggest that all centrioles share a common core,~200 nm in length, but that mammalian centrioles are distally extended.
evidence: The claim is inferred from comparison of mammalian and fly centriole structures.

claim: Fly DMT centrioles are only competent to form sensory cilia
source: Since fly DMT centrioles are only competent to form sensory cilia, whereas mammalian TMT centrioles can form both motile and sensory cilia, it is tempting to speculate that the distal extension endows the centriole with this expanded potential.
evidence: The claim is based on established knowledge about fly centriole function.

claim: Mammalian TMT centrioles can form both motile and sensory cilia
source: Since fly DMT centrioles are only competent to form sensory cilia, whereas mammalian TMT centrioles can form both motile and sensory cilia, it is tempting to speculate that the distal extension endows the centriole with this expanded potential.
evidence: The claim is based on established knowledge about mammalian centriole function.

claim: The distal extension in mammalian centrioles may endow the centriole with the potential to form both motile and sensory cilia
source: Since fly DMT centrioles are only competent to form sensory cilia, whereas mammalian TMT centrioles can form both motile and sensory cilia, it is tempting to speculate that the distal extension endows the centriole with this expanded potential.
evidence: The claim is speculative, based on the structural differences and functional capabilities.

claim: The distal mammalian centriole transitions to a narrower diameter and a geometry more reminiscent of an axoneme
source: The distal mammalian centriole transitions to a narrower diameter and a geometry more reminiscent of an axoneme.
evidence: The claim is based on the structural data showing diameter change and geometry.

claim: The mechanism by which the pinhead terminates at ~200 nm along the centriole from the proximal end is unclear
source: The mechanism by which the pinhead terminates at ~200 nm along the centriole from the proximal end is unclear, but its disappearance along the centriole axis happens quite abruptly indicating that it is precisely determined, rather than developed statistically.
evidence: The claim acknowledges uncertainty about the mechanism while noting the abrupt transition.

claim: The disappearance of the pinhead along the centriole axis happens quite abruptly indicating that it is precisely determined
source: The mechanism by which the pinhead terminates at ~200 nm along the centriole from the proximal end is unclear, but its disappearance along the centriole axis happens quite abruptly indicating that it is precisely determined, rather than developed statistically.
evidence: The claim is inferred from the abrupt transition observed in the data.

claim: Length determination may reside within the cartwheel rather than within the centriole, with cartwheel length being actively controlled
source: One possibility is that length determination resides within the cartwheel rather than within the centriole, with cartwheel length being actively controlled, thereby defining the length of the pinhead-containing region.
evidence: The claim is speculative, proposing a possible mechanism for length determination.

claim: Recent work in the Drosophila embryo shows that cartwheel length is actively regulated
source: Indeed, recent work in the Drosophila embryo shows that cartwheel length is actively regulated (Aydogan et al., 2018).
evidence: The claim is supported by citation to recent work.

claim: The A-tubule MIP that straddles protofilaments A09 and A10 may confer extra stability to the A-tubule
source: A MIP straddling the microtubule seam may confer extra stability to the A-tubule, accounting for the extraordinary stability of centriolar microtubules.
evidence: The claim is speculative, proposing a function for the MIP based on its location.

claim: The larger spacing between protofilaments A09 and A10 may allow the A-tubule to distort creating unique binding sites on the A-tubule
source: The larger spacing between protofilaments A09 and A10 (Figure 1c), may also allow the A-tubule to distort creating unique binding sites on the A-tubule.
evidence: The claim is speculative, proposing a mechanism based on the observed spacing.

claim: Protofilament B01 binds to the lateral surface of protofilament A10
source: Consistent with this idea, protofilament B01 binds to the lateral surface of protofilament A10, suggesting that an A10-B01 lateral interaction may contribute to B-tubule nucleation or stabilization.
evidence: The claim is based on structural observation.

claim: An A10-B01 lateral interaction may contribute to B-tubule nucleation or stabilization
source: Consistent with this idea, protofilament B01 binds to the lateral surface of protofilament A10, suggesting that an A10-B01 lateral interaction may contribute to B-tubule nucleation or stabilization.
evidence: The claim is speculative, proposing a function based on the observed interaction.

claim: Both the canonical- and non-canonical A-C linkers bind to protofilament A09
source: Furthermore, both the canonical- and non-canonical A-C linkers bind to protofilament A09 (Figure 4b and d).
evidence: The claim is based on structural observation shown in Figure 4.

claim: The seam-MIP combination at A09-A10 is a hotspot providing unique sites that contribute to A-tubule functionality
source: Taken together, we believe that this seam-MIP combination is a hotspot providing unique sites that contribute to A-tubule functionality.
evidence: The claim is inferred from multiple observations about the A09-A10 region.

claim: A B01/B02 MIP may enhance construction kinetics of the B-tubule, ensuring its timely construction
source: Given the apparent pause in B-tubule completion observed in the S2 centriole, it seems more plausible that a B01/B02 MIP enhances construction kinetics of the B-tubule, ensuring its timely construction.
evidence: The claim is speculative, proposing a function for the MIP based on observations in S2 centrioles.

claim: The C01/C02 MIP likely plays an analogous role in facilitating efficient initiation and timely completion of the C-tubule
source: The corresponding and similarly shaped MIP at C01/C02 is likely to play an analogous role in facilitating efficient initiation and timely completion of the C-tubule which is necessary for formation of a stable A-C linker.
evidence: The claim is inferred from the similarity to the B01/B02 MIP.

claim: The similar shape and parallel roles of the B and C tubule MIPs suggest that they likely share molecular components
source: The similar shape and parallel roles of the B and C tubule MIPS also suggests that they likely share molecular components.
evidence: The claim is inferred from the structural similarity.

claim: The Y-shaped MIP may correspond to the recently discovered TED complex composed of delta and epsilon tubulins and two accessory proteins
source: An intriguing possibility is that this Y-shaped MIP corresponds to the recently discovered TED complex composed of delta and epsilon tubulins and two accessory proteins (Breslow et al., 2018; Wang et al., 2017).
evidence: The claim is speculative, proposing a molecular identity for the MIP based on recent discoveries.

claim: In the absence of the delta- and epsilon-tubulin complex, centrioles form but are unstable and subsequently disintegrate
source: In the absence of the delta- and epsilon-tubulin complex, centrioles do form, but are unstable and subsequently disintegrate, suggesting that the delta/epsilon-tubulin complex is necessary to stabilize the TMT.
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to recent work on the TED complex.

claim: Delta and epsilon tubulins are absent in Drosophila
source: Consistent with this, these proteins are absent in Drosophila, and S2 centrioles lack those MIPs.
evidence: The claim is based on established knowledge and consistent with the structural observations.

claim: S2 centrioles lack the B01/B02 and C01/C02 MIPs
source: Consistent with this, these proteins are absent in Drosophila, and S2 centrioles lack those MIPs.
evidence: The claim is based on structural observations.

claim: Microtubule stubs reminiscent of those in S2 centrioles have previously been observed in thermally fractionated Sea Urchin DMTs
source: Microtubule stubs reminiscent of those we see in our cryo-tomography data of S2 centrioles have previously been observed in thermally fractionated (40˚ C for 5 min) Sea Urchin DMTs (Linck et al., 2014).
evidence: The claim is supported by citation to previous work.

claim: The possibility that microtubule stubs in S2 data represent damaged or depolymerizing B-tubules cannot be excluded
source: While we did not subject our centrioles to thermal fractionating, we cannot exclude the possibility that the microtubule stubs seen in our S2 data represent damaged or depolymerizing B-tubules that occurs during purification or grid preparation.
evidence: The claim acknowledges an alternative interpretation of the data.
